posts.title: I Built a Stereo Vision Board for Hardware Hackers
posts.description: This article was written entirely by a human, for humans. I tend to get excited about certain chips. This time, it was a microprocessor: The Rockchip RV1103 is a single-core 1.1 GHz ARM Cortex-A7 SoC (system on chip) with 64 MB of DDR2 RAM and a MIPI CSI-2 bus shoved into a QFN-88 package. With this chip, I built a cheap, simple stereo vision board with built-in compute and Linux support.

posts.title: Pick Your Payload - What Open-source Security Hardware Should we Build Next?
posts.description: Everything we do is for educational and ethical purposes only . I build open source hardware that I want, but I won’t work on hardware nobody else wants. If people aren’t fired up, I can’t get excited, so my projects only take off when there’s real interest. I’ve got three ideas, please pick your favourite.
